items.title: Miami Dade College’s The Idea Center and TD Celebrate Entrepreneurs Shaping Miami’s Creative Economy During Miami Art Week
items.text:
Miami Dade College’s The Idea Center and TD Celebrate Entrepreneurs Shaping Miami’s Creative Economy During Miami Art Week

Scale Up Miami, launched in partnership with TD in 2018, has supported more than 500 entrepreneurs through 16 cohorts and expanded in 2025 to include artists
MIAMI (Nov. 25, 2026) – As Miami’s creative economy takes center stage during Miami Art Week , Miami Dade College ’s (MDC) The Idea Center and TD will spotlight the artists and entrepreneurs building businesses behind that momentum through In Practice , a special reception celebrating the intersection of creativity, business and entrepreneurship.
The event will take place Thursday, Dec. 3, from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Bakehouse Art Complex in Wynwood and will showcase the work of participants in Scale Up Miami , The Idea Center’s 12-week business development program for local entrepreneurs.
Presented by The Idea Center in collaboration with TD, In Practice will bring together entrepreneurs, artists and community partners for an evening featuring open studios showcasing the work of Scale Up Miami participants. Guests can also take home an original artwork commissioned for the occasion by Miami-based artist Nicole Combeau , whose work also appears in this season’s broadsheet for MDC’s Museum of Art and Design (MOAD).
Launched in 2018 through a partnership between the TD Charitable Foundation and The Idea Center, Scale Up Miami was created to help local small business owners strengthen their operations, develop sustainable growth strategies and build the skills and connections needed to grow their businesses. Since its inception, the program has trained more than 500 entrepreneurs across 16 cohorts, with continued support from the TD Charitable Foundation and additional funding partners who have joined over the years to expand its reach and impact.
Participants represent a diverse cross-section of Miami’s small business community, spanning multiple industries and neighborhoods. Through a 12-week curriculum, entrepreneurs receive business training, expert instruction, individualized coaching and opportunities to connect with fellow business owners and the broader entrepreneurial ecosystem.
In 2025, Scale Up Miami expanded to include artists in select cohorts, recognizing their potential to build sustainable businesses alongside their creative practices. Made possible through the support of the Wolfson Family , the expansion extends entrepreneurial resources to artists looking to strengthen the business practices behind their creative work and build more sustainable careers.
Bakehouse Art Complex has also helped strengthen the initiative by identifying and referring emerging artists to the program, connecting them with resources that support their professional and business development. Together, the partners are helping The Idea Center make entrepreneurial resources accessible to a broader range of Miami’s business and creative communities.
“At The Idea Center, we believe entrepreneurship takes many forms, and building a thriving business community means creating opportunities for people across industries to turn their ideas and talents into sustainable ventures,” said Jorge Gonzalez, executive director at MDC’s The Idea Center . “Scale Up Miami has helped hundreds of local entrepreneurs strengthen their businesses, and expanding the program to include artists is a natural extension of that mission. items.title: Final Update on Giannis & Embiid's Status as Heat face Philadelphia 76ers: Injuries, Odds, How to Watch
items.text:
The Miami Heat (10-6) and Philadelphia 76ers (14-4) meet for the first of two matchups this regular season. There are more than the usual stakes: the Heat can clinch their group and a spot in the NBA Cup quarterfinals with a win.
Last season the teams split the series, 1-1, with each squad winning on their home floor. But this game will look a lot different than the marquee matchup that was expected when the schedule was released.
The playing status of two players who have won league MVPs was in question heading into the day. In the afternoon, it was announced that Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo was upgraded from questionable to probable while Sixers center Joel Embiid will not be available. Without Embiid, the 76ers will need to rely more on Dean Wade and Adam Bona, but also a group approach to control Antetokounmpo, who has risen to the top five in many MVP ladders.
One key matchup to watch will be the battle of the point guards: Davion Mitchell, averaging 17 points, 8.6 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals, going up against Tyrese Maxey, who is putting up 25.7 points, 5.6 assists, 3.2 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. This will be a challenging road trip for Mitchell, who gets the Knicks' Jalen Brunson and the Cavaliers' Donovan Mitchell next.
The Sixers are most recently coming off a 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers, while the Heat's last game was a 123-113 win over the undermanned Oklahoma City Thunder. That was Philadelphia's first game against a West team all season, while the Heat have already had a West Coast trip. Philadelphia has risen to the top of the East largely on the strength of its clutch play. The 76ers have won the clutch minutes in all 12 games that have entered that territory.
In Miami's most recent game, in which Antetokounmpo did not play, Heat center Bam Adebayo finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists while swingman Pelle Larsson notched 21 points. Miami scored at least 123 points in all five games in its 5-0 homestand, and is stunningly in the top six in offensive rating.
Game date, time and location: Wednesday, Nov. 25, 5:00 p.m. EST, Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

items.title: How Miami Invests in Art Beyond Basel
items.text: Acquisitions, installations, commissions and stipends aimed at local practitioners are all part of the city’s ongoing, year-round efforts to support its homegrown creative community. Most people assume Miami became an “art city” only after Art Basel arrived and turned it into an annual stop on the global art calendar. Yet while the international fair has been instrumental in establishing Miami Art Week and attracting more collectors, the city’s cultural strategy has always extended beyond it. Miami’s institutional commitment to public art predates the contemporary art boom, and the launch of Art Basel Miami Beach , by decades. In 1973, Miami-Dade County established one of the earliest public art programs in the United States, with an ordinance allocating 1.5 percent of the capital costs of new county construction to the acquisition or commissioning of artworks. That made public art part of the civic infrastructure, embedded in the region’s rapid development. You can opt out anytime. Miami-Dade Art in Public Places has since commissioned more than 1,000 works and gained international recognition as a leader in the field. Its artworks are installed countywide at a wide range of sites, including Miami International Airport, Metrorail and Metromover stations, PortMiami, Zoo Miami, the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts, parks, fire stations, libraries, police stations, public housing developments, courthouses and community health centers. The program’s early artworks include a monumental mural by Purvis Young , installed at the Northside Metrorail Station since 1986, and Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen ’s Dropped Bowl with Scattered Slices and Peels , a playful Pop sculpture with a distinctly local nod to Florida’s citrus culture, installed in front of the Stephen P. Clark Government Center. In 1984, Miami Beach created its own Art in Public Places program, which was formalized by ordinance in 1995 and had a similar funding mechanism that initially allocated 1.5 percent of construction costs to public art. “One thing the City of Miami Beach is particularly proud of is that we have been investing in arts and culture for a long time, in different ways. We have cultural grants for cultural institutions and organizations, as well as our investment in Art in Public Places,” Francys Vallecillo , interim director of Miami Beach’s Tourism and Culture Department, tells Observer. “These are programs that run throughout the year. They are not centered on just one week, and they have been a priority for the city for some time.” The program is overseen by the Art in Public Places Committee, a seven-member board appointed by the City Commission that advises the mayor and commission on the selection, commissioning and purchase of artworks. Its acquisition priorities are threefold: to enrich the public art collection, to attract international attention and to celebrate Miami Beach’s diversity and heritage. In September 2019, the City Commission voted to raise the allocation to 2 percent of the hard costs of eligible city projects and to expand eligibility to joint public-private projects. items.title: Man hospitalized after being shot in Kendall, deputies say
items.text:
A man was taken to the hospital on Wednesday after he was shot in Kendall, deputies said.
According to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office, just before 4 a.m., deputies arrived at Southwest 87th Avenue after receiving reports of a person who had been shot.
Deputies said that they then found a man suffering from an apparent gunshot wound, and rescue crews took him to the hospital in stable condition.
Crime scene technicians were spotted outside a home on Southwest 89th Avenue near 118th Street.
One neighbor nearby told NBC6 that she heard about six gunshots around 3:30 a.m.
Detectives spent time gathering evidence in the morning as a K-9 was used to comb the area.
At the home, NBC6 cameras spotted shattered glass and a bullet hole in a window.
The homeowner said he was not injured, and although he was inside the house at the time and ran for cover.
It’s unclear why that person showed up at the house or how he got shot.
No arrests have been made as the investigation remains active.

items.title: Miami-Dade man accused of stabbing his disabled girlfriend multiple times
items.text: MIAMI-DADE COUNTY, Fla. — A 42-year-old man is accused of stabbing his wheelchair-bound girlfriend multiple times during a domestic dispute Tuesday night at their home in Miami-Dade County’s Westchester neighborhood, according to an arrest report. Leer en español Marcos Enrique Sanchez Paz was arrested Wednesday morning and faces one count of attempted felony murder, jail records show. Deputies with the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said they responded to the home around 11 p.m. after receiving a domestic incident-related call involving the couple who had been dating for two years and currently live together. Deputies said Sanchez Paz and the victim were involved in a verbal dispute over “unknown issues” when the argument escalated and Sanchez Paz allegedly grabbed a kitchen knife and stabbed her multiple times. Before being transported to the hospital, the victim, who is a double amputee and uses a wheelchair, spontaneously told deputies, “My boyfriend stabbed me,” according to the report. While lying on the ground, she also FaceTimed her son to tell him that Sanchez Paz stabbed her, the report states. Deputies said the victim was taken by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue medics to HCA Florida Kendall Hospital in critical condition. They said she had to be intubated and rushed into immediate surgery. The report states that the victim suffered a laceration to her spleen, a chest injury, bleeding in her lungs, multiple lacerations to her torso and a broken rib. Deputies said Sanchez Paz fled the scene before they arrived but returned to the scene shortly afterward, where he was taken into custody. The report states that deputies noticed what appeared to be “blood spatter” on his right foot when he was arrested. Sanchez Paz was also transported to a nearby hospital because he was incoherent, the report states. Detectives said he was not interviewed because of his condition and his refusal to provide a statement. As of Wednesday afternoon, Sanchez Paz was being held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center, where his bond was listed as “to be set.” A motive for the stabbing was not immediately clear.

items.title: Miami-Dade man charged with making online threats against Rep. Carlos Gimenez
items.text:
Stephen Nowoczynski made a series of threats on X that were also antisemitic, according to the sheriff’s office.

Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office detectives arrested a man Tuesday who’s accused of making a series of threats on social media last month against U.S. Rep. Carlos Gimenez.
Stephen Nowoczynski, 44, posted multiple statements on X against Gimenez on Oct. 15, threatening the Republican congressman and his granddaughter, police said.
According to the arrest report, in one post Nowoczynski wrote that he would “cut your face in front of your firefighters. I’ll cut your face in front of the sheriff. Where do we put your body?”
Several other posts were antisemitic, one accusing Gimenez of being on “Team Jew,” according to the report.
Miami-Dade detectives were made aware of the posts by Capitol Police investigators, the report states.
Gimenez represents Florida’s 28th Congressional District, which includes southwest Miami-Dade County and the Florida Keys. He released a statement Wednesday saying he and his family “thank federal and local law enforcement for their swift, professional response. Violence of any kind has no place anywhere or any time.”
Deputies arrested Nowoczynski at his apartment on Northwest Second Avenue. According to his arrest affidavit, he admitted making the posts. He was booked into Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center on two counts of making written threats to kill or do bodily harm.
A judge set his bond at $20,000. He is being represented by attorneys with the Miami-Dade Public Defender’s Office.
This story was originally published November 25, 2026 at 1:30 PM .

items.title: Crews put out warehouse fire in SW Miami-Dade; no injuries reported
items.text:
SOUTHWEST MIAMI-DADE, FLA. (WSVN) - Firefighters battled fierce flames after a fire sparked at a warehouse in Southwest Miami-Dade.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the scene of the blaze in the area of Southwest 139th Court and 140th Street, just after 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
Crews arrived to find smoke billowing from an overhead door. Using power tools, Crews they cut into the unit, where they quickly put out the fire.
Firefighters searched nearby units to ensure the flames had not spread.

items.title: Which Miami-Dade and Broward services are closed for Thanksgiving?
items.text:
Thanksgiving is tomorrow, with the federal holiday set to change the way that public services operate in South Florida .
Here's what you should know about county services and schedules in South Florida tomorrow:
Miami-Dade County government offices will be closed on Nov. 26 and Nov. 27.
Solid Waste Management will operate "on a normal schedule," and all disposal facilities "will observe normal operating hours," according to Miami-Dade County's website . Miami-Dade Public Libraries will be closed from Nov. 26 though Nov. 28.
County bus, Metrorail and Metromover services will operate on a "Sunday schedule" on Nov. 26, according to Miami-Dade County .
Metrorail "operates from 5 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week," according to the county . In order to view the schedule for a particular station on a certain day, you can check Miami-Dade County's website .
Broward County government offices will be closed on Nov. 26 and Nov. 27, according to Broward County's website .
The 311 Call Center will be closed, as well as all branches of the Broward County Library. Broward County parks will remain open, " with the exception of Deerfield Island Park and the Parks' administrative offices ." A full list of affected services is available via Broward County .
On Thursday, Nov. 26, Tri-Rail trains will operate on a weekend schedule, according to Tri-Rail's website .
"Trains will not have the flexibility to wait on late comers," Tri-Rail's website states. The company recommends "passengers arrive at the station 20 minutes prior to departure."

items.title: 1836: Dade County is created
items.desc: Dade County was created on February 4, 1836, named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. That same year, Fort Dallas was built and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.
